minutes.headline: Committee approved a lower primary school phone system request; FY2019 school budget outlined, no budget vote yet.
minutes.summary: The meeting opened with a facilities update on how school buildings handled the extreme cold, then a class of 2017 proposal for street pole banners that the committee asked to be reworked with a sustainability plan. The committee approved a revised capital request for the primary school phone system, reviewed the 2018-2019 school calendar, and heard highlights of the recommended FY2019 school budget without taking action. A member was named to the accreditation subcommittee.

public_comment.topic: A resident asked what the extended school year dates mean and questioned why professional development days fall midweek, creating three-day weeks; also commented on banner sustainability.

votes.motion: Approve the revised capital plan: lower the Lunenburg Primary School phone and intercom system request and change the FY2019 total.
Appoint a member as School Committee representative to the NEASC accreditation subcommittee.

Quote came in below the capital plan figure so the request was reduced with a contingency, lowering the capital total.

what_happened.line: The committee approved a revised capital plan that lowers the Lunenburg Primary School phone and intercom request and changes the FY2019 total; the vote count was not audible.
The recommended FY2019 school budget was outlined, with an increase over the current year that adds teachers, a paraprofessional and an assistant principal; no budget vote was taken.
The committee asked the class of 2017 to rework its street pole banner gift with lifespan, labor and sustainability information, and to return in about a month.
The health insurance renewal rate assumed in the budget is not yet known, and last year's rate came in above the budgeted rate.
A member was appointed as School Committee representative to the NEASC accreditation subcommittee.

why_it_matters: The FY2019 school budget request is the figure that will shape the school share of the town budget, mostly taxes, and the health insurance rate is still an open assumption that could move it.
The primary school phone system request was lowered, which reduces the capital total the town is asked to fund for FY2019.
watch_next: The next meeting on February 5th, where the calendar, the budget and the banners are due back as agenda items.
The actual health insurance renewal rate, which budget updates in the superintendent's update will track until the budget becomes an action item.
